title: Autosentry: Near-saturation escape controller with prioritized prober & fallback variants
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a resilient escape controller that triggers automated fallbacks when regional/tier saturation or error signals appear while minimizing noisy cutovers. Unlike previous 'hard' circuit breakers, this ticket implements a prioritized prober that evaluates candidate fallback actions (model variant downgrade, tier shift, or region handoff) using staged probes and tenant-weighted heuristics before committing to a full failover.
motivation: Incidents in Q4 showed repeated brittle failovers where a single spike caused aggressive global variant swaps. Customers with mixed SLAs need quieter, tenant-aware degradations and fewer false-positives that result in unnecessary model variant evictions. We want graceful, reversible actions and rich telemetry for postmortems.
success_metrics: Reduce unnecessary full-variant evictions by 60% in the first month
Decrease P50 customer-request failover latency for degraded flows by 30%
Maintain false-positive fallback rate under 5% per tenant per week
proposal_summary: Introduce Autosentry: a controller combining three capabilities: (1) signal fusion to compute a bounded saturation score from 429s, timeouts, and error-rate windows; (2) a prioritized prober that issues lightweight synthetic requests to candidate alternatives with backoff and local quotas; (3) a staged actuation plan with soft-open, probation, and rollback gates. The controller is tenant-aware and exposes route-level configuration and a console view.
design_notes: Saturation score aggregates: weighted 429 rate (30%), 5xx error rate (40%), timeout ratio (20%), queue-length anomaly (10%). Rolling windows: 10s, 1m, 5m used in ensemble.
Prioritized prober order: local quantized-model -> smaller batch-size variant -> adjacent region (if allowed) -> dedicated reserve pool. Each probe uses a capped token budget and tunable RTT budget.
Actuation steps: soft-open (route-level throttled fallback) -> probation window (1-5m) with enhanced telemetry -> promote to broad fallback or rollback based on pass/fail thresholds.
Per-tenant sensitivity: weight saturation score by recent SLA class and recent probe success rate; enterprise tenants get longer probation and lower sensitivity by default.
Control plane API: new /routing/fallbacks endpoint for route configs and per-tenant overrides. Console dashboard will show active probes and decision traces.

Telemetry: emit decision events with sample payload, probe results, pre/post latency and token-cost deltas, and a unique run_id for each actuation sequence. Include anonymized tenant tag for aggregated metrics.
Fail-safe: a global kill-switch and a tenant-level opt-out flag. Default behavior is opt-in via service-level releases for 10% of routes as canary.
api_changes: GET /v1/route/:id/fallback-status returns active run_id, phase, probe results
acceptance_criteria: Controller evaluates saturation score correctly against test vectors (unit tests)
Prober can exercise model variant and region probes under simulated network faults (integration tests)
End-to-end canary on 10% of traffic shows reduced full-eviction events vs baseline over 48h
Console surface shows run traces and probe outcomes for at least three sample routes
Feature flag with kill-switch validated during chaos run

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Probes could add load and worsen an overloaded route. Mitigation: strict token quotas and randomized probe intervals; probe abandonment under high CPU.
Risk: Wrong weighting yields slower failovers for urgent degradations. Mitigation: emergency fast-path that bypasses probation for hard SLA breach signals.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sampling and aggregated counters with detailed traces only on canary or when debug flag is enabled.
